precepts.text: It grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel. They do not like it when we speak up for our people.
precepts.point: The squeaky wheel gets the oil. We will complain, judge, bring out the records, and beg the Lord until he kills our enemies and sets us up, like the widow before the unjust judge. Our enemies want us silent, locked away with our mouths zipped, calling us troublemakers; yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. Nehemiah 2:10 shows they grieve when a man comes to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
The Lord has set watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem “which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. Watchmen pay attention to the condition of the people and to the enemy coming to destroy the people. “ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.”

Nehemiah shows how the enemy takes it when Israel speaks up: “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” They do not like it when we speak up for our people.

That is why our enemies want us silent, locked away with the key thrown away and our mouths zipped. They call us troublemakers. Yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. They want a quiet slave.

The squeaky wheel gets the oil. Quiet people are ignored, and noisy people force others to take action. So we will complain, judge, bring out the records and tell it like it is, and we will beg the Lord and give him no rest, like the widow before the unjust judge, until he kills our enemies and sets Jerusalem up on high.

precepts.text: The Most High says he will cause the enemy to entreat his remnant well in the time of evil; it is not that the heathen love Israel, but that the Lord moves a king or a friend to deal well with them.
precepts.point: The king grants him all this according to the good hand of his God upon him. Nehemiah had already prayed, and the Most High heard him and put it upon the king's heart to allow him to go.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

precepts.why:
Nehemiah asked the king for letters to the governors beyond the river and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king's forest for timber, “And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.” The Most High had said this would happen: “Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil and in the time of affliction.”

It is not that the heathen love Israel. It is that the Lord causes the enemy to entreat his remnant well in the time of evil and affliction. Nehemiah had already prayed, and the Most High heard him and put it upon the king's heart to allow him to go. The king's favour was the good hand of God, not the king's own goodwill.

precepts.text: Ezra blessed the Most High for putting it into the heart of the king, showing the good the heathen ruler does is the Lord moving him, not his own love for Israel.
precepts.point: The king grants him all this according to the good hand of his God upon him. Nehemiah had already prayed, and the Most High heard him and put it upon the king's heart to allow him to go.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

precepts.why:
Ezra saw the same thing in his day and knew where it came from: “Blessed be the only Lord God of my fathers, who hath put these things into the heart of the king, to glorify his house that is in Jerusalem”.

Ezra did not bless the king; he blessed the Most High for putting these things into the heart of the king. The good the heathen ruler does is the Lord moving him, not his own love for Israel. So when the king granted Nehemiah his letters and his timber, it was “according to the good hand of my God upon me”, the same hand that moved the king in Ezra's day.

precepts.why:
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard that a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, it grieved them exceedingly. This is the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before: “Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building, And hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.”

The people of the land weakened Judah's hands, troubled them in building, and hired counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose, and kept it up from Cyrus to Darius. That same hindering spirit against the rebuilding met Nehemiah the moment he arrived with the king's letters and his escort of captains and horsemen.

precepts.point: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, hear of it, it grieves them exceedingly that a man has come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

precepts.why:
The enemies in Ezra's day wrote to the king: “Be it known unto the king, that the Jews which came up from thee to us are come unto Jerusalem, building the rebellious and the bad city, and have set up the walls thereof, and joined the foundations. Be it known now unto the king, that, if this city be builded, and the walls set up again, then will they not pay toll, tribute, and custom, and so thou shalt endamage the revenue of the kings.”

They called Jerusalem the rebellious and the bad city, and their argument was money: if the walls go up, the Jews will no more pay toll, tribute and custom, and the revenue of kings will suffer. That is the same mindset that fears Israel's rebuilding. Sanballat and Tobiah were grieved exceedingly for the same reason: a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, and Israel restored is a loss to those who profit from Israel down.

precepts.why: “And it came to pass in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that wine was before him: and I took up the wine, and gave it unto the king.” He was the king’s cupbearer, serving the king his wine.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why:
“He that sendeth forth light, and it goeth, calleth it again, and it obeyeth him with fear. The stars shined in their watches, and rejoiced: when he calleth them, they say, Here we be.” This is Christ. “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him” “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

He was at a high estate, because he was in the beginning; that is why he is the Alpha and Omega. “Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is when he brought himself to a low estate as man, because it behoved him to be made like his brethren, so he could take on our afflictions and die for us.

The same way Nehemiah left his great estate because the condition of his people mattered more than himself, Christ left the heavens and came down manifest in the flesh to die for the nation of Israel.

precepts.why:
“For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people.” Mordecai sought the welfare of his people, as Nehemiah did. The Most High always raises up that spark in our brothers to rise up and seek the welfare of their people.

That is why Esau sits around finding ways to give us drugs, crack and cocaine, and to destroy our families and our minds through trauma: so that kind of man will not rise again. The Esthers, the Judiths, the Susannas, the Rebekahs, Shiphrah and Puah: they cannot be allowed to live. But they have all come back. If we are back, they are back, and the nations know it.

points: We was in a Persian captivity, and this is Nehemiah, an Israelite, speaking first person. I took up the wine, and gave it unto the king: that was his occupation. He was the king's cupbearer.

Now I had not been beforetime sad in his presence: it shows you he was a good worker on the job, enthusiastic, optimistic. The purpose of the cupbearer was to pre-taste whatever the king drink, just in case someone tried to poison him. He putting his life on the line every day for a damn heathen king. You think he was in love with that job? No, but he wasn't a slouch. So that one day his countenance was off, it stood out.

note.label: Religious Accommodation

points: Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? The king was able to discern something was terribly wrong. That's how you want to be, brothers and sisters: notable to your employers. The peculiar commandments pertain to integrity and diligence. We're commanded not to be slothful, not with eyeservice but as unto the Lord, whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might. Then your manager is going to take interest in whether you're in a good working condition, because they value your contribution.

note.label: Religious Accommodation

points: Why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste: in chapter 1 you read about Nehemiah praying and fasting to the Lord. This is how the Lord answers our prayers: he put the spirit on the king to inquire what it is that you request.

note.label: Religious Accommodation

points: For what dost thou make request? So I prayed to the God of heaven: that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, that I may build it. That's a hell of a leave of absence right there. That ain't one day off. That's another reason it's important not to be down: the worst that can be said is no. Sometimes you got to go for the gusto. Have faith.

note.label: Religious Accommodation

points: So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time: he put everything in order, got his paperwork straight, and got his leave of absence. points: “Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite”: these two were of other nations. “It grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.”

The other nations always get angry when somebody looks out for the welfare of black people. That’s why they killed Martin Luther King: he was looking out for the welfare of black people. Yet they always have his name in their mouths, asking what Martin Luther King would say, manipulating his speeches to get us to perform. We wouldn’t know, would we? You killed him.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: Everything we went through today you see examples of in the Bible, written before time for our learning. Nehemiah was cupbearer to the king. He saw the state of his people and made his request: “So I prayed to the God of heaven. And I said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers’ sepulchres, that I may build it.”

note.label: State of Decay

points: “For how long shall thy journey be? and when wilt thou return? So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time.” This also shows you dumb apologetics that Isaiah 14 did not happen in the Persian and Median captivity: why would Nehemiah have to ask the king he worked for for leave, if they were already back in the land possessing it?

note.label: State of Decay

points: Nehemiah understood segregation, being separate from the other nations, and here you see the spirit of how the other nations move; they do the same thing today. “Then went I up in the night by the brook, and viewed the wall”, and “the rulers knew not whither I went, or what I did”.

note.label: State of Decay

points: “Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.” He saw the distress of his people. “And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.” They came together as a nation to have their own.

note.label: State of Decay

points: “But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?” The other nations see us building and laugh us to scorn.

note.label: State of Decay

points: “The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.” You, the nations, have no business among us, no business building with us, no business being part of us. Nehemiah understood segregation was what was beneficial for our people, and that these heathen are nothing but trouble.

note.label: State of Decay

points: “Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? this is nothing else but sorrow of heart” … “why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire?” Nehemiah was in great anguish and pain over the destruction of the temple and the walls.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

points: “That thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers’ sepulchres, that I may build it.” Being the king’s cupbearer was a high estate, a high position. But his people were on his mind: the estate of Israel was greater to him than his own estate, so he returned to Jerusalem to build the walls.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

points: “Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian” … “laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?” This is the opposition Nehemiah faced rebuilding God’s walls.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

points: “The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.” That is hard, all praises to the Most High for it. The same thing Nehemiah said is what we need to say today. Christ echoed the same thing with the woman who wanted the blessing for her daughter: he told her no, and only when she answered that even the dogs eat of the crumbs from the master’s table was her daughter healed.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

points: What is Esau out to stop? “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” Sanballat the Horonite was a Moabite, Tobiah an Ammonite.

That is what these nations do not want: the rising of a black Messiah. Their aim is to disrupt, neutralize and destroy any rising of a black Messiah or black Messiahs. Martin King was deemed one, Malcolm was one, Stokely Carmichael, Kwame Ture, was one, Fred Hampton was one. Black unity is deemed a danger to national security; that is why they dissolved us in France. That has not changed.
